title: Roasted Honeynut Squash

items: 2 honeynut squash (about 1 lb each), halved lengthwise and seeded

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment or foil.
Cut each squash in half lengthwise from stem to blossom end. Scoop out the seeds and stringy bits with a spoon. Keep the skin on; it's thin and edible.
Brush the cut sides with the olive oil. Sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Set the halves cut-side down on the pan. Roast 20 to 25 min, until the cut faces are deep golden brown and caramelized underneath.

Flip the halves cut-side up. Put 1 piece of butter in each cavity and drizzle in the maple syrup, if using. Roast 5 to 10 min more, until the butter melts and a fork slides through the thick neck with no resistance.
Serve 1 half per person. Scoop the flesh from the shell with a spoon, or eat the skin too.
tips: Check doneness at the thick neck, since it softens last. Small squash may be done 5 min early.
For cubes, cut the squash into 1-inch chunks with the skin on, toss with the oil, salt and pepper, and roast at 425°F for 20 to 25 min, flipping halfway.
For a savory version, skip the maple and add a pinch of smoked paprika or some chopped fresh sage to the butter.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 4 days. Reheat at 375°F for 10 to 15 min or microwave until hot. To freeze, scoop out the flesh and freeze up to 3 months; thaw in the fridge and reheat.
